transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

Well, I... I guess I'm here because things just haven't been right lately, you know? It's mostly my eating, or I guess, my not eating. What brings me in is I hardly eat right anymore. I mean, I used to be able to sit down and have a real meal, maybe some chicken or rice, but now? Now it's just... I don't even know. Some days it is just coffee. Just cup after cup of black coffee to keep me going, and maybe, if I really force myself, a piece of bread. Just plain bread. I don't even bother putting butter on it half the time because what's the point? It just tastes like ash anyway. And it's really starting to show. My pants, the ones I've worn for years, they're just hanging loose on me. I have to pull my belt to the very last notch, and even then, they feel like they're going to fall right off. It's like I'm just shrinking, and I don't even have the energy to care, but my sister said I looked like a skeleton the other day, and that's when I figured I should probably talk to someone because it's just not normal to live on coffee and a slice of bread, right? It's just... I don't know, it's exhausting just thinking about food.
Are you afraid of gaining weight?

No, no, it's nothing like that. I'm not... I'm not scared of getting fat or putting on pounds or anything like that. Honestly, I wouldn't mind gaining it back. I mean, looking at myself in the mirror right now, it just... it doesn't even look like me anymore. I don't care about the number on the scale at all. Like I said, when my sister called me a skeleton, it actually made me feel pretty awful, you know? It's not like I'm doing this on purpose to fit into some specific size or trying to look good. I don't even buy new clothes, I just wear the same old ones I've had for years. 

It's really just that I don't have the stomach for the food itself. The thought of chewing and swallowing, of actually preparing something and sitting there to eat it... it's just too much work. My brain just says no. So no, I'm definitely not afraid of gaining weight. If someone could just snap their fingers and put fifteen, twenty pounds back on me right now without me having to actually eat a single thing, I'd take it in a heartbeat. I really would. Because being this skinny, it just makes you feel so weak, and I used to be a pretty sturdy guy, you know? I used to be able to do heavy lifting and work with my hands, and now I just feel so drained all the time. So yeah, definitely not about wanting to be thin. I just can't bring myself to eat.
Have you been feeling depressed most of the day?

Yeah, I... I guess depressed is the word for it. It’s just this constant, heavy feeling, you know? Like, almost every single day, I wake up and before I even open my eyes, I can feel it sitting right there in the middle of my chest. Just this huge, empty weight. It's like... it's like I already know the day is going to be pointless before my feet even hit the floor. I just lie there thinking about how there's absolutely nothing good waiting for me out there. Nothing to look forward to, nothing that makes me want to get up and actually do anything. 

I used to wake up and at least think about, I don't know, maybe going for a walk or fixing something around the house, but now? Now I just want to pull the covers up over my head and keep my head down. It’s like the world is just too loud and too much, and I just want to disappear into the mattress. I’ll just lay there for hours sometimes, watching the sunlight move across the wall, and I don't feel anything except that emptiness. It’s not even sadness, exactly, it’s just... flat. Just completely hollowed out. And it stays with me all day. Even if I do manage to drag myself up to get that cup of coffee I was talking about, that heavy feeling just follows me into the kitchen, sits with me at the table... it just never really lifts. So yeah, most of the day, almost every day, it’s just... it’s just really dark and heavy.
Have you been having thoughts that life isn’t worth living?

No... no, I wouldn't say that. I mean, I know I just sat here and told you how empty everything is, and how I just stare at the wall all day, but... I don't sit there thinking life isn't worth living. It's more just... I don't know how to live it right now. I've never been the type to think about checking out early, you know? 

Even when things got really bad before, like when I couldn't find work anymore, or way back when I was a kid and left school in the middle of junior high... things were tough, really tough, and I didn't have much going for me, but I always figured you just gotta keep going. You just take what you get and deal with it. And I still feel that way, deep down, I guess. It's just that right now, just existing takes all the energy I've got. So, no, I don't have those kinds of thoughts about it not being worth it. I don't look around the house and think about ending it or anything like that. 

I just... I just wish the days weren't so incredibly long. I wish that heavy feeling would just lift off my chest, but I definitely don't want my life to go away. It's a weird difference, I guess, wanting to just hide under the covers and disappear from the noise of the world, but not wanting to actually be gone for good. But that's exactly how it is for me. I just want to sleep until the emptiness stops, not... not be dead. So no, I haven't been thinking anything like that.
Did all this start after something stressful happened in your life?

No, not really. I mean, I've been trying to figure that out myself, honestly. You'd think there would be some big, dramatic event, right? Like someone dying, or getting into a terrible accident, or losing a house... something you could point to and say, "There, that's when everything went wrong." But it wasn't like that at all. 

I've been out of work for a while now, and yeah, that's stressful, but it's been a constant kind of stress, you know? It's not like I just got fired yesterday and suddenly I can't get out of bed. It's just been this slow, grinding reality for years. And like I said, I left school way back in junior high, so I've never exactly had an easy time of it. I've always just sort of scraped by, doing odd jobs, fixing things... just making do. So it's not like my life was suddenly turned upside down by some new, terrible thing.

It was more like... it just sort of crept up on me. Like the weather changing. One day you're fine, maybe a little tired, and then a week later you realize you haven't seen the sun in days and you're freezing. I just woke up one morning and that heavy feeling was there, and it just never left. I've sat there in my bed, staring at the wall, just racking my brain, trying to think if someone said something to me, or if I saw something on the news, or if I ate something weird... I mean, you look for any explanation when you feel this bad. But there's nothing. No big fight with my sister, no sudden bills I couldn't pay... just nothing. It's incredibly frustrating, actually, because if there was a reason, maybe I could fix it, you know? If I knew what broke, I could try to put it back together. But this... it just feels like my brain decided to shut down all on its own, without even asking my permission or waiting for a reason.
Have you lost interest in things you usually enjoy?

Yeah... yeah, I definitely have. It's actually one of the things that bothers me the most, if I'm being honest. Because, you know, I don't have a lot going on. I'm not working, I don't have this big busy life. But I always had my things, you know? Little things that kept me occupied and made me feel decent. 

Like, I used to really like walking by the lake. There's this spot not too far from my place, and I'd go down there in the mornings or late afternoons when the sun was hitting the water just right. I'd just walk, maybe sit on this one bench I liked, watch the ducks or whatever... it was peaceful. It gave me a reason to get out of the house. And then, when I was inside, I've always been into building these little model kits. Cars, mostly, sometimes airplanes. I started doing it years ago, just something to do with my hands. I’d set up at the kitchen table, get my glue and my tiny little paints, and I could sit there for hours, just focused on getting the decals exactly straight or making the engine block look realistic. It was satisfying, putting something together piece by piece. 

But now? Man, I haven't been down to the lake in... I can't even tell you how long. The thought of putting my shoes on and walking down there just seems exhausting. Like, what's the point? The water's just water. And my models... I've got this one, a '67 Mustang, sitting half-finished on the table. It's been sitting there for weeks, maybe months. I walk past it every day, and I just look at it, and it's like... it's like it belongs to somebody else. Like I don't even recognize the guy who started building it. I look at the little pieces still on the plastic sprue, and I feel absolutely nothing. No desire to pick up the glue, no interest in seeing it finished. It’s just clutter on the table now. 

It’s really strange, how something that used to hold my attention so completely just... doesn't register anymore. I tried to sit down and work on it one day, maybe a week ago, thinking maybe if I just forced myself, the feeling would come back. But I just stared at the instructions for twenty minutes, feeling that heavy emptiness in my chest, and then I just went back to bed. So yeah, I've lost interest in everything. It's all just... blank.
Have you been moving or speaking noticeably slower than usual?

Yeah... actually, yeah. My sister, she comes over sometimes to check on me, right? Because she knows I've just been sitting around not doing much of anything. And she got really frustrated with me the other day. She asked me... I think she just asked me if I wanted her to heat up some soup or something. Just a really simple question. And I heard her, I knew exactly what she said, but... it was like my brain just couldn't get the words down to my mouth. It takes me a really, really long time to answer even a simple question lately. I just sat there staring at the floor, and she was sort of waving her hand in front of my face like, "Hello? Are you in there?" 

And it's not just the talking, either. It's my whole body. She actually said to me, she goes, "You look like you're walking through mud." And honestly, that's exactly what it feels like to me, too. Like the air in my apartment got really thick all of a sudden, like I'm trying to move underwater or through molasses or something. Just getting up from the edge of the bed to go to the kitchen... it takes so much effort just to lift my leg, and then put it down, and then lift the other one. I just sort of shuffle along. 

I feel so incredibly heavy all the time. Everything is just playing out in slow motion. Even when I try to hurry up, like if someone knocks on the door and I want to answer it before they leave, I just... I can't. My body just won't do it. It's like I'm wearing a lead suit. So my family definitely notices it, yeah. They look at me like I'm an old man or something, just because it takes me five minutes to cross the room or to finally spit out a "yes" or a "no" when they talk to me. It's just... it's exhausting, trying to push through that mud all day.
